newsitem.title: USA: Victim of apparent racial beating out of coma.
newsitem.headline: Victim of apparent racial beating out of coma.

text.p: A 13-year-old Chicago boy who was the victim of an apparent racially motivated beating awoke from a coma Friday, a Cook County Hospital spokesman said.

Lenard Clark sustained severe head injuries after he was knocked off his bicycle and beaten a week ago, allegedly by three white teens who later bragged that they were keeping blacks out of their South Side neighbourhood.
"He has continued to show signs of improved motor abilities and increased responsiveness," John Reyes, media coordinator at Cook County Hospital, said.

The three teens, two high school students at De La Salle Institute aged 17 and 18 and a recent graduate aged 19, were charged with attempted murder and committing hate crimes. They remained free on bond.
Defence lawyers said the three did not participate in the attack and were arrested by police in what they called a rush to judgment because of the case's highly charged nature.

A second day of protests and a peace march led by black community leaders was planned Friday near where Clark was attacked in Bridgeport, a traditionally Irish American neighbourhood. Few blacks live in Bridgeport although an increasing number of Asians and Hispanics have moved there.
